title: Ranking the cornet players in the Dimes band
summary: Vincent lists cornetists in order: Dimes, Blue, William Padjo, Ricard Ellis, Willie Edwards, George McCullen, Alba Du Conger, plus Chris Kelly.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: . And we had this fellow, William Padjo. You can get him. Yeah, yeah. We had him, right? He was going to school at that time. But he was a good reader, but he couldn't jazz. So we got Ricard Ellis. And then Willie Edwards, we had Willie Edwards. Then we had George McCullen for a little while. I forget this fellow. I wanted to spell it, but I thought I could remember. Du Conger. I couldn't make it out.
Du Conger? Yeah, yeah, Du Conger. Yeah, yeah, Alba Du Conger.
Alba. You know him, eh? You heard talk of him. Alba Du Conger. They tell me the policeman in Chicago.
First was Wesley Dunn. Yeah, and second was Blue. Yeah. And third was who? What's the man this? No, ask him who the third corner.

Who was the third corner player? William Padjo. William and Ricard Ellis was the fourth. Oh, huh. And then Willie Edwards was the fifth. George McCullen was the sixth. Albert Du Conger, he was the seventh. Chris Kelly, he was another good corner player. You hear what I'm talking about? And then I played by the fellow with the third. And then Johnny Henry with the third. And then I went with Punch, you see? After Punch quit Jack Carey, where he was taking Jack's whole band. He played with him. Ask him if you played with Jack.
